name: Zolpidem Tartrate
meta: Psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985 and Schedule H/H1 of the Drugs &
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder (tartrate); melting point 193–197 °C; sparingly soluble in water.
Generic since 2007; the most widely prescribed 'Z-drug' hypnotic. Onset ~30 minutes after an oral tablet. First approval/introduction: Europe 1988 (Synthélabo); US FDA 1992 (Searle).

Selective agonist at the alpha-1 subunit-containing GABA-A receptors (benzodiazepine-1 site), producing hypnotic effect with little anxiolytic, muscle-relaxant or anticonvulsant activity. Receptor / target profile: Positive allosteric modulator selective for alpha-1-containing GABA-A receptors (Ki ~27 nM), producing hypnotic effect with weak anxiolytic/myorelaxant activity.
Summary: Bioavailability ~70%; rapid onset (Tmax ~1.6 h; slower with food). ~92% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4. Half-life ~2.5 h (longer in elderly/hepatic impairment).
